subject: anatomy
title: Embryonic Renal Systems and Ureteric Bud Induction

steps.tx: The human urinary system develops from intermediate mesoderm, which forms three successive bilateral excretory systems displaying cranial-to-caudal succession during intrauterine life: the pronephros, mesonephros, and metanephros. The **pronephros** appears early in the fourth week as nonfunctional vestigial nephrotomes in the cervical region, regressing completely by day twenty-five.
steps.say: The urinary system develops from intermediate mesoderm in three successive waves: the pronephros, mesonephros, and metanephros. The pronephros appears in week four as nonfunctional cervical clusters that degenerate completely by day twenty-five.

vis.alt: Pronephros, mesonephros, and metanephros succession with ureteric bud
vis.caption: Sequential development of pronephric, mesonephric, and metanephric systems. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: As the pronephros regresses, the **mesonephros** forms in the thoracolumbar intermediate mesoderm. It features functional glomeruli and tubules that produce small amounts of urine between weeks six and ten before degenerating. Its excretory conduit, the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct, persists in males to form the epididymis, ductus deferens, and seminal vesicles.
steps.say: As the pronephros regresses, the mesonephros forms in the thoracolumbar region. It possesses functional glomeruli that filter urine temporarily. In males, its drainage duct, the Wolffian duct, persists to build the epididymis, vas deferens, and seminal vesicles.

steps.tx: The definitive adult kidney develops from the third system, designated the **metanephros**, originating in the sacral intermediate mesoderm during the fifth week. Development of the metanephros requires reciprocal induction between two embryological primordia: the epithelial ureteric bud and the surrounding metanephric blastema.
steps.say: The adult kidney develops from the metanephros in the sacral region during week five. Metanephric organogenesis requires reciprocal molecular induction between two tissue components: the epithelial ureteric bud and the surrounding metanephric blastema.

steps.tx: The **ureteric bud** arises as a diverticulum from the posterior wall of the mesonephric duct near its entrance into the cloaca. Penetrating the metanephric tissue cap, it undergoes repeated dichotomous branching to form the entire collecting system: the ureter, renal pelvis, major calyces, minor calyces, and one to three million collecting ducts.
steps.say: The ureteric bud sprouts from the mesonephric duct near the cloaca. Penetrating the metanephric cap, it branches repeatedly to construct the collecting system: ureter, renal pelvis, major and minor calyces, and millions of collecting tubules.

steps.tx: The **metanephric blastema** represents the condensed sacral intermediate mesenchyme surrounding the branching ureteric bud tips. Under induction from the bud ampullae, blastemal cells undergo mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition, forming renal vesicles that elongate into S-shaped nephron tubules to create Bowman capsules, proximal tubules, loops of Henle, and distal convoluted tubules.
steps.say: The metanephric blastema consists of sacral intermediate mesoderm surrounding the bud tips. Stimulated by the bud, these cells convert into epithelial nephron tubules, creating Bowman capsules, proximal convoluted tubules, loops of Henle, and distal tubules.

steps.tx: During the sixth to ninth weeks, the developing kidney undergoes **renal ascent** from its initial pelvic position in front of the sacrum up into the lumbar retroperitoneal fossa immediately beneath the suprarenal glands. This cranial ascent is driven by longitudinal elongation of the fetal torso and unbending of the caudal body curvature.
steps.say: Between weeks six and nine, the kidney undergoes cranial ascent from the pelvis in front of the sacrum to the upper lumbar fossa below the adrenal glands. This migration is driven by bodily elongation and uncurling of the fetal spine.

vis.alt: Renal ascent, pelvic kidney, and anomalous renal vessels
vis.caption: Renal ascent from pelvic origin and arterial laddering. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: As the kidney ascends, its arterial supply changes continuously through a succession of transient lateral splanchnic arteries sprouting from the aorta. Lower embryonic vessels degenerate as higher ones form. Persistence of lower embryonic vessels produces **accessory renal arteries**, which typically enter the lower pole and can kink the ureteropelvic junction.
steps.say: During ascent, the kidney receives blood from temporary lateral branches of the aorta. Lower vessels degenerate as higher ones form. Persistent embryonic vessels become accessory renal arteries, which enter the lower pole and can obstruct the ureter.

rows: Common iliac or middle sacral artery
Single renal artery at L1-L2 level

steps.tx: If a kidney fails to ascend out of the true pelvis, it remains as a congenital **pelvic kidney**, lying adjacent to the common iliac artery and anterior to the sacral promontory. Bilateral renal agenesis occurs when ureteric buds fail to develop, leading to lack of fetal urine production, severe oligohydramnios, and fatal Potter sequence.
steps.say: Failure of ascent leaves a congenital pelvic kidney near the common iliac artery. Bilateral renal agenesis occurs when ureteric buds fail to sprout, causing severe oligohydramnios, pulmonary hypoplasia, and fatal Potter sequence.

left.title: Pelvic Kidney Findings
points: Kidney lodged in true pelvis near sacrum
Supplied by iliac or lower aortic branches
Possesses short ureter entering bladder normally
Normal renal function in absence of obstruction

right.title: Renal Agenesis / Potter Sequence
points: Complete failure of ureteric bud induction
Absent fetal urine causes severe oligohydramnios
Severe pulmonary hypoplasia is cause of death
Facial dysmorphism with flattened nose and low ears
